name: Seletracetam
summary: Seletracetam (UCB 44212) is a pyrrolidone-derived drug of the racetam family that is structurally related to levetiracetam (trade name Keppra). It was under development by UCB Pharmaceuticals as a more potent and effective anticonvulsant drug to replace levetiracetam but its development has been halted.

pharmacology.text: Seletracetam's anti-epileptic effects are due to its high affinity binding to synaptic vesicle glycoprotein 2A (SV2A)—part of a calcium ion regulator. The SV2A protein assists with the coordination of synaptic vesicle exocytosis, which induces neurotransmitter release in the presence of an influx in Ca2+.

uses.text: It was under development by UCB Pharmaceuticals as a more potent and effective anticonvulsant drug to replace levetiracetam but its development has been halted.

fact.en: Seletracetam is a close relative of levetiracetam, a widely used epilepsy drug. Both bind SV2A, a protein on the sacs that hold neurotransmitters, a target found only because levetiracetam was there first.
